name: retro
short: Reviews a finished agent session, finds where time or tokens were lost, and proposes setup fixes, worst first.
what: retro walks through one agent session and lists every friction moment: long searches, repeated failures, user corrections, expensive calls that returned little. It reads your repo's steering files, checks and CI, sorts each moment into a category like guardrail, navigation or skill, and proposes one change per moment ranked by severity. It changes nothing until you pick which ones to apply.
who: People who run coding agents on a repo often and want each run to go better than the last. If you only use an agent now and then, it's more process than you need.
needs: A coding agent that loads skills

steps.title: Install the dev workflow bundle
steps.text: retro is part of this bundle.

steps.title: Or use the Skills CLI
steps.text: The README's project install command for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor.
steps.code: npx skills add shipshitdev/skills --agent claude-code codex cursor

steps.title: Run it at the end of a session
steps.text: The skill doesn't trigger by itself. Call it with `/retro`, and add `--deep` for a long or messy session.

watch: It only proposes changes. Anything it applies, such as new hooks, CI jobs or lint rules, needs your confirmation.
The README warns not to use `--all` with the Skills CLI, since that installs to 30+ agents.
